paper.title_en: Brane-world gravitational atoms: Massive quasi-bound states of the Casadio–Fabbri–Mazzacurati black hole
paper.abstract_en: Massive fields can remain trapped for long times outside a black hole, forming clouds with discrete energies much like electrons in an atom. We study these clouds around the Casadio–Fabbri–Mazzacurati brane-world black hole, whose time geometry is the same as in the Schwarzschild solution but whose radial geometry carries a possible imprint of an extra dimension. We find that the cloud energies change only slightly as this deformation is varied, whereas their lifetimes are much more sensitive. Spherically symmetric clouds decay faster as the deformation grows, while clouds with angular structure decay more slowly, with a stronger effect at higher angular momentum. This contrasting behavior arises because the radial deformation changes the effective distance and barrier separating a cloud from the horizon. More massive fields are more tightly bound, whereas higher radial excitations remain farther from the black hole and live longer. Two independent numerical methods reproduce the known Schwarzschild and weak-binding limits. The clouds are metastable, with lifetimes governed by absorption at the event horizon. The results therefore identify cloud lifetimes as a more sensitive probe of the brane-world geometry than the level energies alone.
